title: How Does Credit Supply Expansion Affect the Real Economy? The Productive Capacity and Household Demand Channels
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; data/design; results/mechanism; conclusion
teaching_function: Opens with two rival real-economy channels and orders U.S. and international evidence around their distinct price-and-quantity predictions.
transfer_limit: The tradable-nontradable discriminator and deregulation instruments are setting-specific; do not label every credit boom a supply shock.

title: The Loan Covenant Channel: How Bank Health Transmits to the Real Economy
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; data/design; results/mechanism; conclusion
teaching_function: Turns apparently long-maturity credit into a renegotiation puzzle and links covenant breaches lender health commitment cuts and real outcomes.
transfer_limit: Covenant leverage and confidential supervisory data are unusual; the long front matter is not a default template.

title: FinTech Credit and Entrepreneurial Growth
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; data/design; results/mechanism; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses an algorithmic cutoff to connect FinTech credit to firm growth and organizes mechanisms around information asymmetry and collateral scarcity.
transfer_limit: The proprietary platform cutoff and digital-footprint advantage do not transfer automatically; opacity heterogeneity alone is not a mechanism test.

title: How Much Does Racial Bias Affect Mortgage Lending? Evidence from Human and Algorithmic Credit Decisions
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data/design; selected results; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates observed denial gaps algorithmic recommendations unobserved underwriting risk and differential treatment before stating a bounded conclusion.
transfer_limit: Algorithmic recommendations are not a universal race-neutral benchmark and the evidence supports bounds rather than absence of discrimination.

title: Banking on Deposits: Maturity Transformation without Interest Rate Risk
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; data; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Reverses the textbook premise states the deposit-franchise hedge mechanism and maps aggregate and cross-bank evidence to its predictions.
transfer_limit: Deposit-market power and the sample period delimit the hedge result; do not infer that all banks are immune to rate risk.

title: The Forced Safety Effect: How Higher Capital Requirements Can Increase Bank Lending
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; calibration; predictions; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds a countervailing mechanism in which tighter capital can raise lending and uses calibration to show when the sign changes.
transfer_limit: The sign reversal is model- and calibration-dependent; it is not a reduced-form estimate of a particular capital reform.

title: Bank Funding Risk, Reference Rates, and Credit Supply
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; data; calibration; welfare; conclusion
teaching_function: Connects credit-line drawdowns wholesale funding benchmark design deposits and welfare through a full balance-sheet mechanism.
transfer_limit: Large-bank regulatory data and assumed drawdown-deposit behavior limit extrapolation to smaller banks and nonbank credit lines.

title: Access to Collateral and the Democratization of Credit: France’s Reform of the Napoleonic Security Code
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; design; results; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a legal collateral reform to move from credit access to firm outcomes entry geography and allocation while keeping treatment explicit.
transfer_limit: The civil-law reform and fixed-asset exposure are setting-specific and are not a generic collateral instrument.

title: Loan Terms and Collateral: Evidence from the Bilateral Repo Market
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; data/design; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Distinguishes collateral screening bargaining and loan-term incidence in bilateral repo with institutional detail and contract-level tests.
transfer_limit: Repo collateral and bargaining institutions are specialized; do not transfer predictions to ordinary corporate loans without justification.

title: Barter Credit: Warehouses as a Contracting Technology
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; identification; mechanisms; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Treats storage as a contracting technology and orders evidence from debt capacity to competing mechanisms and real outcomes.
transfer_limit: A single agribusiness lender and warehouse technology bound external validity; staggered adoption does not solve every placement concern.

title: Relationship Trading in Over-the-Counter Markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; model; fit; counterfactuals; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines network facts with a structural relationship model while making repeat business and execution speed do distinct jobs.
transfer_limit: The welfare result depends on estimated preferences and an insurer-dealer network; unbundling does not generally lower welfare.

title: Inventory Management, Dealers’ Connections, and Prices in Over-the-Counter Markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; predictions; simulation; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds price formation from inventories and core-periphery connections and states interaction predictions rather than using generic centrality.
transfer_limit: This is primarily a theory lesson with simulation; connectedness must not be treated as exogenous empirical variation.

title: Do Municipal Bond Dealers Give Their Customers “Fair and Reasonable” Pricing?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional setting; measurement; results; regulation; conclusion
teaching_function: Begins with same-bond same-day price dispersion validates strategic-pricing measures and evaluates whether dealer rules change markups.
transfer_limit: Municipal retail trades and strategic-price measures are specialized; same-day dispersion alone does not establish exploitation.

title: Decentralized Exchange: The Uniswap Automated Market Maker
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; protocol; framework; data; comparison; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains a new venue from protocol primitives and compares AMM and limit-order mechanisms using exhaustive transaction data.
transfer_limit: Blockchain observability does not remove wash trading gas fees token quality or off-chain comparison problems.

title: Fire-Sale Spillovers and Systemic Risk
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; framework; estimation; decomposition; validation; conclusion
teaching_function: Converts a fire-sale sequence into a measurable vulnerability index and decomposes buildup into leverage adjustment illiquidity and concentration.
transfer_limit: The index is scenario-based vulnerability rather than observed causal contagion; calibration choices must remain visible.

title: A Model of Systemic Bank Runs
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; equilibrium; amplification; policy; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses linked creditor-coordination and interbank-price layers to explain systemic amplification and orders sections around the feedback loop.
transfer_limit: The equilibrium mechanism is not direct evidence that a historical crisis followed the modeled path.

title: Liquidity Transformation and Fragility in the U.S. Banking Sector
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; theory; measurement; results; alternatives; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines transformation and fragility separately turns run predictions into deposit-flow tests and challenges information alternatives.
transfer_limit: Flow-performance sensitivity can reflect information; the conclusion requires the full battery of alternative tests.

title: Resource Allocation in Bank Supervision: Trade-Offs and Outcomes
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; data; identification; counterfactuals; conclusion
teaching_function: Treats supervisory hours as a scarce input estimates technology and revealed preferences and reserves counterfactual language for the model.
transfer_limit: Revealed preferences are model-dependent and should not be recast as normative priorities or causal welfare estimates.

title: Lender Automation and Racial Disparities in Credit Access
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; design; mechanisms; alternatives; conclusion
teaching_function: Prestates cost capacity geography and human-bias channels and assigns distinct evidence blocks to each explanation.
transfer_limit: PPP had government guarantees and emergency processing; automation effects need not generalize to ordinary underwriting.

title: The Dark Side of Circuit Breakers
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; predictions; empirical analysis; welfare; conclusion
teaching_function: Pairs equilibrium theory with transaction data to show how a stabilizing rule can create a magnet effect and conditional welfare losses.
transfer_limit: Empirical patterns support predictions but do not identify the whole welfare model; breaker design differs across markets.

title: On the direct and indirect real effects of credit supply shocks
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; identification; channels; conclusion
teaching_function: Constructs lender-specific shocks before network exposure and separates direct effects downstream propagation trade credit and prices.
transfer_limit: Estimated shocks and input-output propagation rely on rich Spanish links; network exposure is not automatically exogenous.

title: Sorting out the effect of credit supply
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; motivating facts; model; implementation; decomposition; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses bank-borrower sorting as the motivating fact and quantifies how the distribution of bank costs changes aggregate lending.
transfer_limit: The aggregate decomposition is structural and sorting-specific; it should not replace design-based estimates elsewhere.

title: How does competition affect retail banking? Quasi-experimental evidence from bank mergers
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; design; prices/quantities; substitution; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses an antitrust threshold then reports deposit prices mortgage quantities small-business nulls and nonbank responses together.
transfer_limit: The threshold and remedy institution are specific; product nulls and nonbank adjustment warn against one competition effect.

title: A quantitative analysis of bank lending relationships
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; facts; model; estimation; validation; counterfactuals; conclusion
teaching_function: Estimates relationship demand and uses model fit untargeted validation and competitive counterfactuals to quantify amplification.
transfer_limit: Counterfactuals inherit the loan-demand system and model closure; do not present them as model-free evidence.

title: Bank transparency and deposit flows
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; measurement; results; policy shock; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from construct validity to depositor flows funding costs profitability and a policy shock while keeping implications distinct.
transfer_limit: Transparency is constructed and much analysis is observational; policy claims should remain calibrated.

title: Market power in wholesale funding: A structural perspective from the triparty repo market
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; facts; model; identification; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds repo facts before the model states identifying variation and translates dealer markdowns into funding spreads.
transfer_limit: Triparty money funds and dealers are a niche; markdowns should not be generalized to all repo markets.

title: Liquidity regulation and banks: Theory and evidence
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; reduced form; model; welfare; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines regulatory evidence with a heterogeneous-bank model to trace risk reduction lending crowd-out migration and welfare.
transfer_limit: Treatment and structural welfare depend on thresholds and assumptions; keep evidence layers labeled.

title: Collateral and asymmetric information in lending markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; model; estimation; counterfactuals; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses contract choice to distinguish adverse selection from moral hazard and clarifies why collateral can reveal rather than merely secure risk.
transfer_limit: Collateral selection here does not imply that collateral always signals high or low borrower quality.

title: Why are commercial loan rates so sticky? The effect of private information on loan spreads
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; empirical design; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Frames sticky spreads as an information problem and aligns within-relationship variation with that mechanism.
transfer_limit: The evidence is about information and repricing in commercial lending; do not call all rate rigidity inefficiency.

title: Screening using a menu of contracts: A structural model for lending markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; estimation; fit; counterfactuals; welfare; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a contract menu to make screening operational documents fit and reports allocation and welfare under stated structure.
transfer_limit: Welfare depends on menu restrictions and estimated types; model fit does not validate every counterfactual.

title: Dealers’ insurance, market structure, and liquidity
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; comparative statics; calibration; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes dealer insurance the primitive and organizes liquidity implications around mechanism-specific comparative statics.
transfer_limit: The mechanism is model-based; liquidity labels must match the dealer-insurance margin.

title: The electronic evolution of corporate bond dealers
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional change; data; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Treats electronification as a change in dealer intermediation and compares execution inventory and customer access across regimes.
transfer_limit: Electronification coincides with other changes; avoid treating adoption as randomly assigned.

title: Price-setting in the foreign exchange swap market: Evidence from order flow
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; data; price setting; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Links FX swap quotes to order flow and balance-sheet constraints after defining the price-setting object.
transfer_limit: Order flow may reflect information and hedging; interpretation requires institutional timing.

title: Siphoned apart: A portfolio perspective on order flow segmentation
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; empirical implications; welfare; conclusion
teaching_function: Explains segmentation through correlated order-flow portfolios so inventory management drives venue predictions.
transfer_limit: The result depends on correlated flows and common market makers; it is not a universal argument for segmentation.

title: Corporate bond mutual funds and asset fire sales
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; identification; null evidence; conclusion
teaching_function: Challenges a familiar claim defines fundamental-value pressure carefully and puts identification and null evidence before limits.
transfer_limit: A carefully identified null does not show that bond funds can never create fire-sale pressure.

title: Anatomy of a liquidity crisis: Corporate bonds in the COVID-19 crisis
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; crisis timeline; market participants; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a timeline to narrate shifting securities trade-size pricing inventories and liquidity providers without one omnibus spread.
transfer_limit: COVID and Federal Reserve intervention are exceptional; descriptive anatomy is not a single-shock causal design.

title: Monetary tightening and U.S. bank fragility in 2023: Mark-to-market losses and uninsured depositor runs?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; methodology; framework; scenarios; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines asset valuation with uninsured funding and a run framework while separating exposure assumptions and aggregate risk.
transfer_limit: Mark-to-market and run estimates are scenario calculations rather than realized systemwide losses.

title: Swap Trading after Dodd-Frank: Evidence from Index CDS
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; message data; model; results; conclusion
teaching_function: Starts from a venue mandate explains RFQ and order-book protocols and links dealer exposure to execution outcomes.
transfer_limit: SEF rules and index CDS are specialized; message exposure is not execution quality everywhere.

title: The death of a regulator: Strict supervision, bank lending, and business activity
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; design; channels; real outcomes; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses regulator extinction then traces management capitalization lending and local activity as distinct channels.
transfer_limit: The OTS transition bundles authority and organization; channel tests do not all share equal causal strength.

title: Price regulation in two-sided markets: Empirical evidence from debit cards
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; background; design; incidence; substitution; conclusion
teaching_function: Follows regulation around both platform sides and quantifies bank recovery card substitution merchant incidence and welfare limits.
transfer_limit: Two-sided substitution is central; merchant savings or lower regulated prices alone cannot establish welfare.

title: Monetary Transmission through Shadow Banks
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; data; model; mechanism; conclusion
teaching_function: Contrasts regulated and shadow intermediaries through clienteles and links policy to deposit substitution and fragility.
transfer_limit: Money-market funds are the operative shadow deposits; do not extend the result to every nonbank intermediary.

title: Bank Cleanups, Capitalization, and Lending: Evidence from India
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; design; mechanisms; real outcomes; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses an asset-quality review to show why disclosure without recapitalization can induce underinvestment and zombie lending.
transfer_limit: The Indian review lacked a capital backstop; effects need not match cleanup programs with recapitalization.

title: The Rise of Finance Companies and FinTech Lenders in Small Business Lending
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; new data; design; substitution; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds lender-type data before testing whether nonbank expansion offsets bank contraction in quantities and outcomes.
transfer_limit: UCC coverage and the postcrisis window matter; offsetting quantities do not prove equivalent borrower welfare.

title: Nonbank Lending and Credit Cyclicality
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; data; composition tests; model; conclusion
teaching_function: Compares banks and nonbanks over cycles uses matched borrowers to separate supply from composition and explains funding cyclicality.
transfer_limit: Syndicated lending and government-supported bank funding define the comparison; it need not apply to all products.

title: How Did Depositors Respond to COVID-19?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; design; alternatives; conclusion
teaching_function: Pairs branch deposit rates with quantities and alternatives to give a disciplined account of precautionary saving.
transfer_limit: Local infections affect many behaviors; interpretation depends on within-bank comparisons and alternative tests.

title: Shocked by Bank Funding Shocks: Evidence from Consumer Credit Cards
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; identification challenges; data; incidence; conclusion
teaching_function: Names the supply-demand challenges before estimation and reports limits substitution capacity borrowing and incidence sequentially.
transfer_limit: The shock occurs in credit-card limits; do not generalize incidence to mortgages or business lending.

title: Banks as Liquidity Multipliers
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; equilibrium; results; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Derives the liquidity multiplier from joint asset and deposit choices and conditions stability implications on the model.
transfer_limit: The multiplier is a theorem under stated primitives rather than an empirical money multiplier estimate.
metadata_note: Final publication year 2024; recovered from the 2023 source-folder package.

title: Safe Collateral, Arm’s-Length Credit: Evidence from the Commercial Real Estate Market
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; shutdown design; matched results; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a market shutdown to test an ex ante matching model of collateral and creditor type and compares distress outcomes.
transfer_limit: The CMBS shutdown and matching assumptions are particular to commercial real estate.

title: Fintech Borrowers: Lax Screening or Cream-Skimming?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; screening; ex-post outcomes; conclusion
teaching_function: Asks lax screening versus cream-skimming and separates borrower selection from post-origination performance.
transfer_limit: Comparisons remain vulnerable to unobserved selection; higher default is not by itself proof of lax screening.

title: Collateral Effects: The Role of FinTech in Small Business Lending
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; matching/IV; mechanisms; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from a 13 percent credit response to investment pledging alternatives and an IV making complementarity the mechanism.
transfer_limit: Matching and shift-share evidence have different assumptions; pledging is mechanism evidence not randomization.

title: Liquidity Provision Contracts and Market Quality: Evidence from the New York Stock Exchange
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; contract; RDD; liquidity dimensions; placebos; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a contract discontinuity and reports depth spreads price improvement off-exchange effects and placebos together.
transfer_limit: The NYSE threshold need not transfer to markets without off-venue provision.

title: Institutional Order Handling and Broker-Affiliated Trading Venues
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; matched designs; execution quality; conclusion
teaching_function: Addresses routing conflicts with discretion matched brokers matched child orders and an external venue constraint.
transfer_limit: Routing discretion and affiliation are setting-specific; correlations alone should not be called causal.

title: OTC Intermediaries
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; regulatory data; calibration; dealer exit; conclusion
teaching_function: Calibrates a core-periphery network to positions and makes dealer exit and risk-bearing the counterfactual objects.
transfer_limit: Dealer-removal results depend on calibrated network and cost structure; they are not forecasts of a named failure.

title: When Do Low-Frequency Measures Really Measure Effective Spreads? Evidence from Equity and Foreign Exchange Markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; measurement; validation; applications; conclusion
teaching_function: Validates spread proxies against high-frequency benchmarks and turns measurement failure into empirical guidance.
transfer_limit: Proxy performance varies with spread-to-volatility ratio; do not discard all low-frequency measures.

title: Liquidity Restrictions, Runs, and Central Bank Interventions: Evidence from Money Market Funds
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; setting; data; mechanisms; intervention; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows how state-contingent gates create complementarity and uses microdata to distinguish the run from stabilization.
transfer_limit: The COVID run and 2016 rule are distinctive; prose cannot separate every crisis policy.

title: Self-Fulfilling Fire Sales: Fragility of Collateralized Short-Term Debt Markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; equilibrium; policy; conclusion
teaching_function: Develops a collateralized-debt run without sequential service and compares policies inside the equilibrium framework.
transfer_limit: Policy rankings depend on the global-games equilibrium and collateral market; they are not treatment effects.

title: Bond Price Fragility and the Structure of the Mutual Fund Industry
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; framework; data; mechanisms; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Starts from internalization derives concentration predictions and uses trading prices mergers and policy evidence to narrow the channel.
transfer_limit: Concentration may proxy for active views; mechanism requires merger and policy variation beyond baseline correlation.
metadata_note: Final publication year 2024; recovered from the 2023 source-folder package.

title: The Effect of Bank Supervision and Examination on Risk Taking: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; background; natural experiment; alternatives; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a geographic relocation as a supervision-capacity shock and orders risk taking failure fiscal cost and alternatives.
transfer_limit: The historical relocation is unusual; identical regulation does not ensure identical local shocks.

title: From Market Making to Matchmaking: Does Bank Regulation Harm Market Liquidity?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; comparative statics; robustness; welfare; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows regulation shifting dealers from market making to matchmaking through distinct competition immediacy cost and welfare margins.
transfer_limit: The welfare reversal requires bank power plus internal and external competition; regulation does not generally improve liquidity.

title: Digital Payments and Consumption: Evidence from the 2016 Demonetization in India
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; identification; mechanisms; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses demonetization to induce adoption reports first stage and magnitude early and rules out four competing channels.
transfer_limit: Demonetization cash dependence and supermarket transactions define the estimand; the channel may differ elsewhere.
